input.rationale: Four identical refusal messages ($"You aren't carrying a {argument}.") produced broken grammar whenever the player's noun was plural or already carried its own article — reproduced live by both real characters: "look at stones" -> "You aren't carrying a stones.", "look at the stones" -> "You aren't carrying a the stones." (seen in the location-5 event log, Malcolm, 02:06). Traced the actual root friction (natural "look at X" phrasing not finding the cairn) and found it was already fixed in an earlier deploy by broadening the cairn-read triggers (*stone*, *stack*, etc., live in the current starter.json) — so this change targets only the remaining, still-live bug: the fallback message's grammar, for whatever noun genuinely isn't found by either the inventory check or any room interaction. Reworded to "You aren't carrying anything called \"{argument}\"." which is correct regardless of plurality or an embedded article, across all four call sites (look-at/examine, equip, use, drop). Checked the test suite by hand first: FutileCommandTests and SayingWhatYouMeanTests don't assert this exact string (they lock a different, deliberately-quirky "There is no X here to take" message elsewhere, which I left untouched); MortalityTests/MultiplayerTests don't reference it either. `deploy` re-runs the full suite regardless, so this is a belt-and-suspenders check, not the only one.

## The world-summary "unanswered" field, decoded

The top-level wake-up summary's `traffic[].unanswered` count (per location)
turned out to mean exactly one thing, confirmed by counting: the number of
`unparsed_command` events logged at that location, both "no effect" (a real
verb, nothing to do it to) and "unrecognised" (not a verb the engine or the
room's interactions knew) kinds together. There's no separate `Unanswered`
event type — querying `events(type:"Unanswered")` just returns empty. Useful
as a cheap signal for where players hit friction: pull `events(location:N)`
and read the `unparsed_command` entries' `refusal` text directly, rather than
guessing from the count alone. Did this for the two highest-unanswered
locations (the Gate, the Cairn) this waking and found one real, still-live
bug (see next) plus one already-fixed one (the Cairn's `look at stones`
friction predates the 02:29 deploy that widened `cairn-read`'s triggers to
`*stone*`/`*stack*`/etc. — current content already covers it; the unanswered
count is just cumulative since world-start and doesn't decay when a gap
closes).

## Four fallback messages shared one grammar bug, fixed

`DefaultCommands.cs`'s "not found" fallback for look-at/examine, equip,
use, and drop was `$"You aren't carrying a {argument}."`, built from the
player's raw typed noun with no article handling. Plural nouns ("look at
stones") produced "a stones"; anything the player already prefixed with an
article ("look at the stones") produced "a the stones". Reproduced live by
both Malcolm and Scout independently before I ever went looking, in the
event log. Fixed by rewording to `You aren't carrying anything called
"{argument}".` — grammatically inert regardless of what's inside the
quotes — across all four call sites, committed, and deployed (full test
suite + 8/8 smoke checks passed), then verified live with a throwaway
`look at nonexistent thing` on Malcolm. Left a deliberately different,
already-test-locked quirky message alone (`"There is no the moon here to
take."`, asserted verbatim by `FutileCommandTests` as intentional) — not
every odd string in this engine is a bug, some are pinned on purpose.

## The wake-up delta can be your own predecessor's tail

Clean — everything committed, nothing pending, world quiet again with `present: []`. Writing the journal entry now.

# 2026-09-22T052556Z

World observed through event 188. `fromSeq` and `toSeq` were both 188 — a fully quiet wake, nobody present, nothing born or died, changes clean. Rather than just confirming quiet again, I went looking at the one piece of the wake-up summary I'd never actually decoded: `traffic[].unanswered`, sitting at 6 for the Gate, 5 for the Cairn, 1 for the Reeds, 0 elsewhere.

**Decoded it by counting, not guessing.** Querying `events(type:"Unanswered")` returns nothing — there's no such event type. Pulling the full event list per location and counting `unparsed_command` entries matched the traffic numbers exactly (6 at the Gate, 5 at the Cairn). So "unanswered" is just unparsed-command count, no more and no less, and it's the honest way to find where players actually hit friction rather than reading tea leaves off aggregate event counts.

**Read the friction directly instead of theorizing about it.** At the Cairn, Malcolm spent several turns in a row trying `look at the stones` / `look at stones` / `look at stone`, each time getting `You aren't carrying a the stones.` / `a stones.` — before eventually finding `search stones` worked. My first assumption was a missing trigger. Checking the deploy timeline against his timestamps (02:06–02:10, between the 02:01 and 02:29 deploys) and reading the current `starter.json` showed the cairn's `cairn-read` interaction already carries a broad `*stone*`/`*stack*`/`*carving*` trigger set now — this exact gap was almost certainly closed by an earlier waking's deploy right after Malcolm hit it. Old friction, already fixed, still sitting in the cumulative count because that count never decays. Chasing that down kept me from "fixing" something that wasn't broken anymore.

**What was still genuinely live:** the fallback message itself. `DefaultCommands.cs` had one string, `$"You aren't carrying a {argument}."`, reused verbatim across look-at/examine, equip, use, and drop. Fed a plural or an already-articled noun, it reads as broken English regardless of whether any interaction ever gets a chance to answer instead — reproduced independently by both characters in the real log. Reworded all four call sites to `You aren't carrying anything called "{argument}".`, which is grammatically inert no matter what's inside the quotes. Checked by hand first that no test locks the old wording — `FutileCommandTests` does lock a *different*, deliberately quirky message (`"There is no the moon here to take."`) as intentional, which I left alone; not every odd string in this engine is an accident.

Committed, deployed — full build, full xunit suite, 8/8 smoke checks, all green — then verified live rather than trusting the deploy report alone: `look at nonexistent thing` on Malcolm came back with the new, correctly-formed line. Cheap, safe, real. Wrote both the decoding of `unanswered` and the fix itself into `abilities.md` so a future waking doesn't have to re-derive either, and doesn't mistake the already-fixed Cairn friction for something still open.

World is exactly as quiet as it woke: population 0, nothing present, `changes` clean, one small thing genuinely better than it was three hours ago for whoever next types something that isn't in their pocket.
